marks.note: 'prendere' is acceptable: 'prendere la colazione' is standard Italian (dictionaries give fare colazione / prendere la colazione; hotels say 'la colazione si prende in sala'). Replace prendere with a verb that is truly impossible here, e.g. 'dare' or 'tenere'.
'fare' forms an established phrase with another meaning: 'il salato fa sete' (makes you thirsty), alongside 'mettere sete'. Replace fare with e.g. 'tenere' or 'stare'.

'essere' is acceptable: 'essere di fretta' (sono di fretta = I'm in a hurry) is very common standard Italian with the same meaning, and 'non c'è fretta' is everyday. The calque essere is therefore not a clean error; either drop the row or keep essere only with an exercise sentence that excludes 'di' (better: drop).

'essere' occurs in the standard impersonal 'c'è bisogno di' (esserci bisogno), same meaning. In a personal-subject gap sentence ('Io ___ bisogno di aiuto') essere is wrong, but the profile requires wrong in every reading. Keep only if the gap sentence has a personal subject; otherwise replace.

'essere' is acceptable in another reading: 'sono freddo' = I am cold to the touch / emotionally cold ('sei freddo, hai le mani gelate'; 'è una persona fredda'). The gap sentence must force the 'feel cold' reading; as a bare pair the distractor is not unacceptable in every reading.

'portare' forms an established phrase: 'portare l'attenzione su qualcosa' (direct attention to), common in instructions and writing. Replace portare with e.g. 'dare' (dare attenzione is also marginal, so better 'mettere' or 'tenere').

'sciogliere' is acceptable: 'sciogliere un problema / un quesito / un dubbio' = risolverlo is listed in Treccani and used in formal writing. Replace sciogliere with e.g. 'fissare' (the real English-speaker calque of 'fix') or 'correggere'.

'dire' is acceptable: 'dire scusa' / 'Di' scusa alla signora!' is everyday native usage with the same meaning (it is exactly English 'say sorry'). Remove dire (and from calque); the English-speaker calque of 'apologise' is not available, so leave calque out or use 'fare' as first distractor. en should be 'to apologise'.

'aprire' is not what an English speaker produces ('open the light' is not English; 'aprire la luce' is a southern Italian regionalism). The English calque of 'turn on / put on the light' is 'girare' or 'mettere'; put that first and in calque.

'chiudere' is not an English calque ('close the light' is not English; 'chiudere la luce' is a southern regionalism). English 'turn off / switch off' gives 'girare' or 'fermare'/'staccare'; set calque accordingly (fermare is already listed).
'potente' is not an English calque: 'strong coffee' maps word-for-word to 'caffè forte', which is correct, so there is no calque; leave calque out (and the pair is a weak trap for English speakers).
'grande' is not an English calque: 'high fever' maps word-for-word to 'febbre alta', which is correct. Leave calque out.
'grande' is not an English calque: 'high season' maps to 'alta stagione' directly. Leave calque out.
'completa' is not an English calque: 'full' is 'pieno' in every bilingual dictionary, so English speakers say 'luna piena'. Leave calque out.
'grande' forms an established phrase: 'una grande pressione' (great pressure, physical or figurative: 'sotto grande pressione'). Replace grande with e.g. 'grossa' or 'larga'.

'parlare su' is accepted in formal/lecture use ('parlerà sulla crisi economica', cf. 'una relazione su'), so 'su' is not cleanly wrong. A cleaner calque is hard to find; consider dropping english_calque by setting differs_from_english false, or keep with certain=false.

'a' is also standard with some nouns for the same meaning: entrare a scuola, entrare al cinema, entrare a teatro (and 'da' for the point of entry: entrare dalla finestra). The profile says to leave out heads where the preposition is not fixed; drop the row or restrict to nouns that take 'in' (in casa, in macchina, nel negozio).
'pagare per' is correct Italian: 'Quanto hai pagato per quella borsa?', 'pagare per i propri errori'. The calque is not genuinely wrong; drop the row or set differs_from_english false.

For 'believe in' (existence) 'a' is equally standard: credere ai fantasmi, credere agli UFO, credere a Babbo Natale; 'in' dominates for faith/values (credere in Dio, nella giustizia). Two prepositions for the overlapping meaning; narrow en_pattern to 'to have faith in sb or sth' or drop.
'per' is also standard with a noun of cause: 'sono contento per il risultato', and the only option for the person one is happy for ('sono contento per te'). Not a fixed single preposition.

'a' is standard, not a calque error: 'bravo a tennis', 'bravo a scacchi', 'bravo a calcio', and colloquially 'bravo a scuola / a matematica'. Both in and a are used for 'good at'; drop or restrict to school subjects and change calque.
'per' is equally standard before an infinitive: 'Siamo pronti per partire', 'pronto per uscire'. Two prepositions, same meaning: drop the row per the profile.
'Ti invito a cenare da noi sabato' is grammatical but natives say 'Ti invito a cena da noi sabato' (noun). Use an infinitive that is natural here: 'Ti invito a venire da noi sabato.'
Not full: in computing 'libreria' (software library) is the standard current term, listed in Treccani. Should be partial (note the profile itself cites libreria as full).

Not full: 'gentile' also means delicate, refined in current use ('lineamenti gentili', 'il gentil sesso', 'un fiore gentile'), which overlaps 'gentle'; partial. The trap is also mild (kind vs gentle), close to the profile's 'no harm' exclusion.
The usual Italian for 'palace' is 'palazzo' itself (Palazzo Reale, Palazzo Ducale, Palazzo Pitti); 'reggia' is only a royal residence. Correct value: 'palazzo reale' (or palazzo).
The row's own en_meaning lists 'inclusive (of)' ('prezzo comprensivo di IVA'), which is the 'including everything' sense of comprehensive; that is a shared sense, so partial, not full.
Not strictly full: 'lettura' also means a lecture/talk in academic use ('lettura magistrale', 'letture dantesche'; Treccani: conferenza su un autore o un'opera). Partial.

'romanzo' does cover the literary genre 'romance' ('romanzo cavalleresco', 'romanzo cortese' = medieval romance), and English 'romance' also means a romance novel ('romanzo rosa'). Partial rather than full.

'attendere a' = attend to, see to ('attendere ai propri doveri, alle faccende'), a current dictionary sense shared with English 'attend (to)'. Partial; it_for_lookalike 'frequentare' fits only school/course, 'partecipare a' for events.
English 'sympathetic' also means likeable ('a sympathetic character'), which is exactly 'simpatico' ('un personaggio simpatico'). The main senses differ but one is shared: partial.

Says 'essere when intransitive'. Intransitive vivere takes essere OR avere in standard Italian ('ho vissuto a Roma tre anni' is at least as common as 'sono vissuto'); dictionaries give aus. essere o avere. Correct note: 'Avere with a direct object (ha vissuto una vita felice); intransitive: essere or avere, both standard (è vissuto / ha vissuto a Roma).' auxiliary_choice must accept both for intransitive use.

spec_notes: collocations: 'every wrong_collocate unacceptable in every reading' cannot hold for verb_noun pairs with a concrete noun, because any transitive verb gives a compositional reading (prendere una foto = pick up a photo; avere un viaggio = have a trip coming up; prendere la spesa = collect the groceries). The rule needs restating as 'unacceptable with the meaning in the gap sentence', and the exercise sentence must fix that meaning.

collocations: 'put the English calque first and repeat it in calque' pushes authors to invent a calque where English maps word-for-word to the correct Italian (caffè forte, febbre alta, alta stagione, luna piena, pressione alta, prezzo alto). Such pairs carry no English-speaker trap and should be excluded, or calque must be explicitly absent.

collocations: avere + bodily-state nouns (freddo, caldo) collide with essere + adjective (sono freddo = I am cold to the touch / cold-natured), so the essere calque is acceptable in another reading; the profile's every-reading rule makes the core light-verb rows it asks for first formally impossible unless the gap sentence carries the disambiguation.

collocations: phrases needing an extra preposition (essere di fretta, esserci bisogno, arrivare all'obiettivo) are not addressed: say whether a distractor that is correct only with an added preposition counts as acceptable.

verb_government: preposition choice that depends on the noun (entrare in casa / a scuola; andare in / a) has no slot; the profile's 'leave out' rule applies but authors do not apply it. State it explicitly for motion verbs.

false_friends: kind is defined only from the Italian side ('never has the lookalike's meaning'); secondary senses of the ENGLISH word (sympathetic = likeable, attend to, romance = novel genre) also create overlap. The profile's own 'full' example libreria has a current computing sense (software library), so the example contradicts the definition.

false_friends: for partial rows whose shared sense IS the lookalike's main meaning (palazzo/palace), it_for_lookalike 'the usual Italian for the lookalike' is the lemma itself; the profile should say whether that is allowed or such rows excluded.
noun_gender: gender_cue for monosyllables in -e (re, tè) - literal reading gives e_ending, but the plural is invariable because it is monosyllabic; 'other' would teach better. Ambiguous.

noun_gender: plural_type for la mano / le mani is 'regular' by the letter of the rule (-o to -i), although the feminine -i plural is something learners must memorise; the profile should say explicitly.

verb_conjugation: past participles in -iuto (conosciuto, piaciuto, giaciuto) insert i to keep the sound; the profile does not say whether this is a spelling adjustment (regular) or a participle irregularity. The rows treat it as regular, which I accept.

verb_conjugation: auxiliary 'both' asks for a note on 'when each is used', but for vivere (and often iniziare, cambiare in some uses) intransitive use itself admits both; the note format should allow 'both, either' for intransitive.
patterns: A 'wrong' partner or english_calque that is in fact acceptable standard Italian, often with a small change in construction: essere di fretta, c'è bisogno, prendere la colazione, dire scusa, pagare per, bravo a, pronto per, contento per, credere a, entrare a, parlare su (12 rows).

Calque field filled with a word an English speaker would not produce: regionalisms (aprire / chiudere la luce) or arbitrary non-calques where English maps directly (potente, grande x2, completa) (6 rows).
false_friends kind 'full' where a current secondary sense overlaps, on the Italian or the English side (libreria, lettura, attendere a, simpatico, comprensivo, romanzo, gentile) (7 rows).
Distractors that form an established phrase with another meaning: grande pressione, portare l'attenzione su, fare sete, sciogliere un problema, sono freddo (5 rows).
Form tables (noun_gender, verb_conjugation) are essentially clean; the only fault is an oversimplified auxiliary_note (vivere).
